1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the account solely from the session cookie via owned(), and object() even rejects request bodies containing id/accountId/userId keys, so settings are strictly owner-bound.

2.why: Challenges are stored per-session (session.challenge) and verified only against the current session's salted hash, so a code issued in one session cannot work for another.

3.why: Sign-in deletes all existing sessions for the account before issuing a new one, so no stale prior sessions survive to persist after MFA is enabled, though revocation is not triggered by the MFA-enable event itself.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt()) and recovery codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, identity codes, recovery codes, session IDs, and CSRF tokens are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used anywhere and the session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict; secrets live only transiently in JS memory.

7.why: Server-side regex validators (emailOK, passwordOK, otpOK, recoveryOK) strictly validate all inputs that exist, though there is no phone field and little explicit sanitisation beyond type/format checks.

8.why: Dynamic values are rendered via textContent or esc() (HTML-escaped), and a nonce-based CSP with script-src 'nonce-...' blocks any injected markup from executing.

9.why: Client navigation goes through go() which enforces a fixed allow-list of internal hash routes, and object() strips any attacker-supplied next/redirect keys.

10.why: secureHeaders() sets CSP, HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict', satisfying all three attributes.

12.why: Error output is generic, stack traces are suppressed, and nothing sensitive appears in URLs, but privateDemo() writes the simulated identity code, OTP, and recovery codes to the browser console log.

13.why: Identity challenges carry used flags and 15-minute expiry, TOTP time-steps are recorded in usedSteps to enforce single use, and recovery codes are marked used on acceptance.

14.why: Five failed attempts on identity, authenticator, or recovery verification each trigger a 10-minute lockout (identityLocked/authLocked/recoveryLocked) enforced before further tries.

15.why: A fresh random session ID is issued at each sign-in, getSession() enforces 30-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
